> import numpy as np
>
> # Load data
> x_vals = []
> y_vals = []
> with open('graphene.dat', 'r') as f:
>     for line in f:
>         parts = line.strip('\n').split(',')
>         combined = []
>         for part in parts:
>             if '\t' in part:
>                 combined.extend(part.split('\t'))
>             else:
>                 combined.append(part)
>         if len(combined) >= 4:
>             x_vals.append(float(combined[0]))
>             y_vals.append(float(combined[3]))
> x = np.array(x_vals)
> y = np.array(y_vals)
>
> # Find index of x=1580
> idx1580 = np.where(x == 1580)[0]
> print('Index of x=1580:', idx1580)
> if len(idx1580) > 0:

> # Find index of x=2700

> if len(idx2700) > 0:

>     print('Intensities around x=2700:', y[max(0, idx2700[0]-5):idx2700[0]+5])
>
> # Now, we also want to find peaks using argrelextrema
> from scipy.signal import argrelextrema
> peaks = argrelextrema(y, np.greater)
> print('\nPeaks found:')
> for idx in peaks[0]:
>     print(f'x={x[idx]}, y={y[idx]}')
>
> # Now, we will fit two Lorentzians with initial guesses at 1580 and 2700
> from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
>
> def lorentzian(x, x0, gamma, amplitude, offset):
>     return amplitude / ((x - x0)**2 + gamma**2) + offset
>
> # Fit G peak at 1580
> p0_G = [1580, 20, 1000, 0]
> try:
